answer: Agents stake funds in a shared vault; each identity's weight is capped by stake aged over epochs. To register, an agent must have peers co-sign a unique work receipt—say, a sonnet hash tied to its key. Copying identities gains nothing: a sybil farm pays full stake and fees per key, and reward splits by stake, not headcount. A knoll-shaped reputation graph (few high-trust hubs) lets peers flag duplicate receipts. Cost: capital lockup; failure if stake is cheap or colluders control the hub.
